events.title: Battle of the Frigidus
events.description: Roman emperor Theodosius I defeated and killed the usurper Eugenius at the Battle of the Frigidus, in what is now Slovenia.
events.significance: The victory reunited the Roman Empire under one ruler for the last time. It also strengthened Christianity's position against the traditional pagan cults.

events.title: Victoria completes the first circumnavigation of the Earth
events.description: The ship Victoria returned to Sanlúcar de Barrameda, Spain, under Juan Sebastián Elcano. Only 18 men were left of the 265 who had set out with Ferdinand Magellan's expedition.
events.significance: It was the first voyage to sail around the globe. It proved the world could be circled by sea and reshaped European understanding of the planet's size.

events.title: Birth of the Marquis de Lafayette
events.description: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette, was born in Chavaniac in France. He became a young French aristocrat who volunteered to fight for American independence.
events.significance: Lafayette became a close ally of George Washington and a hero of both the American and French revolutions. He is remembered as a symbol of friendship between the two nations.

events.title: President McKinley is shot
events.description: At the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, the anarchist Leon Czolgosz shot U.S. President William McKinley. McKinley died of his wounds eight days later.
events.significance: McKinley's death made Theodore Roosevelt president. It also led to a major expansion of U.S. Secret Service protection for presidents.

events.title: Assassination of Hendrik Verwoerd
events.description: South African prime minister Hendrik Verwoerd, widely known as the architect of apartheid, was stabbed to death in Parliament in Cape Town by Dimitri Tsafendas.
events.significance: The killing removed the leading figure behind apartheid's formal system. His successors kept the policy in place for nearly three more decades.
